clues.text: When Agabus foretold a great famine, the Antioch disciples sent relief to the elders in Judea with him and Saul.
At Paphos, the proconsul Sergius Paulus summoned this man and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
Writing to Corinth, Paul asked whether he and this man were the only apostles who must work for a living.
When the Jerusalem disciples were afraid of Saul, this man brought him to the apostles and spoke for him.
After Paul healed a lame man at Lystra, the crowds called this man Zeus and called Paul Hermes.
He and Paul argued so sharply over taking John Mark that they parted, and he sailed to Cyprus.
Paul wrote that when Peter stopped eating with Gentiles at Antioch, even this companion was led astray.
